findings.summary: One bullet holds two ideas: replica promotion and replication lag.
findings.evidence: "Replica can be promoted to a standalone DB; lag is possible"
findings.fix: Split it into "Replica can be promoted to a standalone DB" and "Async replication means replica lag is possible".

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "configurable", "transaction").
findings.evidence: Automated backups: a daily snapshot plus transaction logs, on by default with 7 days of retention (configurable 1-35). Point-in-time restore works to any second within the window. Setting retention to 0 turns them off.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The mistake about disabling backups on a source with read replicas gives no reason, so a skimming learner cannot tell why it is a mistake.
findings.evidence: "Disabling backups on a source with read replicas"
findings.fix: Add the reason, for example "Retention 0 on a source breaks replication, since replicas need its backups/logs".

findings.summary: The cheat sheet and quiz say a Multi-AZ standby serves no reads, but page 1 says the Multi-AZ DB cluster standbys do serve reads, so the unqualified claim is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Page 5: "Reads | None | Yes"; page 6: "No: the standby serves no reads; it only waits for failover." Page 1: "Multi-AZ DB cluster (two readable standbys) is the exception: standbys serve reads"
findings.fix: Qualify the claim as "Multi-AZ instance: standby serves no reads (DB cluster is the exception)" on pages 5 and 6, or name the Multi-AZ instance deployment explicitly in the tables.
